note: Every sensor is a make target and nothing else. The Makefile is already the single definition of what CI runs (R1.13); binding sensors to it means humans, CI and agents share one vocabulary, and a gate cannot be strengthened in one place and quietly left behind in the others. If a sensor here would need a command that is not a make target, the target is what is missing.

stack.stackNote: The bootstrap scan reported typescript as primary and found no Docker and no build tools. It had indexed experiments/ and the browser SDK only — the Go service under services/collector/internal was absent from its map entirely. Corrected by hand rather than preserved: a harness that describes the wrong repository is worse than none.

sensors.name: gofmt clean
sensors.description: Every Go source is gofmt -s clean. Formatting is never litigated in review here.

sensors.name: race suite
sensors.description: go test -race across both modules. The api package drives real HTTP rather than calling handlers directly, because v1 lost a provenance chain to a field-name mismatch that every in-memory test survived.

sensors.name: golangci-lint
sensors.description: Core defect-class set only (.golangci.yml). Every linter guards a class of bug, not a preference — a config that fires on style teaches people to read red as noise.

sensors.name: govulncheck
sensors.description: Reachable advisories in both modules. go.mod pins toolchain go1.26.5 as the security floor.

sensors.name: generated artifacts match their sources
sensors.description: libs/genproto from schemas/, contract/openapi.yaml from the Go wire types, contract/fixtures/ from the harness wire modules. All three are committed and drift-gated; none may be edited by hand.

sensors.name: OpenAPI specification lint
sensors.description: Curated vacuum ruleset (.vacuum.yaml), failing on warnings. It has already caught a schema demanding every field of a discriminated union, and a published example outside its own enumeration.

sensors.name: experiment harness syntax and asserted selftests
sensors.description: py_compile, node --check, the statistics selftest (22 assertions) and the numbers-schema fixture corpus (21 fixtures). No browsers, no network — the part of the harness that is checkable on every push.

sensors.name: go.mod tidy
sensors.description: Runs against copies and restores the originals, so the check never mutates the tree it is judging.

sensors.name: coverage measured
sensors.description: Reported, never thresholded. -coverpkg so the wire-level tests get credit for the packages they actually drive. A threshold would become a number to satisfy; this figure exists to be looked at.

sensors.name: the whole gate
sensors.description: Everything CI runs, in the order CI runs it. `make ci` green locally and a green pipeline are the same statement — that equivalence is the reason the Makefile exists.

sensors.name: the six numbers
sensors.description: THE project invariant, and deliberately outside `make ci`: it needs real browsers and takes about seven minutes. Required after any change touching services/, experiments/ or schemas/. The target now MEASURES AND CHECKS: it compares the run against the newest manifest in docs/results/ and fails on a rate outside the baseline's Wilson interval in either direction, a tier that has gone missing, p99 over the 80ms budget, a cold start that blocks, a false-positive rate that lost its value, or a >10% memory regression. The comparison logic is itself asserted by experiments-check, inside `make ci`, where it needs no browsers. Tiers 5 and 6 are seeded (GT_SEED), so their figures are repeatable; a moved number with no explanation is indistinguishable from a broken detector.

sensors.name: the product runs end to end
sensors.description: Drives the path a visitor actually takes — the host page, sdk.js from the collector, the cross-origin session handshake, telemetry, the stream, the snapshot the engine judges from, the server-to-server decision the host application makes, and the archive's durable position — with a real browser inside the compose network, asserting all seven links by name. The other topology sensors enter the chain in the MIDDLE with bodies they build themselves; nothing else here loads the page or runs the SDK, and the two failures this catches were both WIRING that left every service healthy and every request answered. It brings its own topology up in a compose project of its own, so unlike the sensors below it needs nothing running first and cannot inherit a system another gate just took apart.

sensors.name: collector and engine agree
sensors.description: A/Bs the collector against the decision engine over real HTTP while both are up, and checks the demo host is wired to the engine rather than to itself. The two services mount the SAME decision package (ADR-0005); what differs is where the state came from — memory versus the KV snapshot — so a disagreement here is libs/snapshot losing something the judgement needed. Also compares the tenant-registry fingerprint both services publish, because two processes that disagree about who exists each behave correctly alone and wrongly together.

sensors.name: each service taken away
sensors.description: Stops each service in turn and checks the promise the contract makes about its absence: the collector decides from memory with the engine gone, the demo host fails OPEN rather than breaking, an outcome REFUSES rather than lying about durability, and — since PR-5.1 — a decision comes back promptly rather than after the broker's own ack timeout. That latency assertion found a second unbounded path on its first run.

sensors.name: the books balance under an outage
sensors.description: The Phase 3 gate: drive traffic, induce a broker and an archive outage, and reconcile against the archive's DURABLE position rather than against process counters. Every record the collector accepted must be in the archive, refused on purpose, or named as unaccounted. Twenty-five records per scenario — it proves the accounting is sound and says nothing about rate, which is what makes it cheap enough to run automatically.

sensors.name: the accounting holds under load
sensors.description: The Phase 4 gate: sustained concurrency, the accounting still balancing, the decision p99 inside its budget. DELIBERATELY NOT AUTOMATED, unlike the three above. It measures RATES, and a rate measured on a shared runner encodes that runner — this repository learned that twice in one pull request, when a CI machine reported an inlined commit at 48/s against 18 244/s locally, and moved its timing assertions to `make measure` for exactly this reason. Run it on a machine whose numbers mean something, and commit the manifest.

sensors.name: the capture protocol runs without a human
sensors.description: Drives synthetic participants through the real two-service capture path and checks three things: the protocol runs at all, every participant produces one labelled row, and the cohort labels (arm, condition, visit) never cross the wire — only the participant code does, as subject_id. The third is a claim experiments/README.md makes and nothing checked. Governs the ONE published number that is null, so its failure mode is a study that cannot start rather than a number that moves.
